statement: For the kinematic embedding (14), dimension is N(N+1)/2. Put D(m)=2^(m−1)det[binom(2(m−i−j),m−2i)] for 1≤i,j≤floor(m/2), the ordinary matrix degree of SO_m. Theorem 5.1 proves deg(SE_N)=D(N+1) for odd N; its proof yields deg(SE_(2k))≤D(2k+1)−2^(k−1)D(2k). These degrees count generic complementary affine linear sections of this specified embedding.

answer.display: D(N+1) for odd N; ≤D(2k+1)−2^(k−1)D(2k) for N=2k

source.location: Eq. (15), Theorem 5.1 and inequality immediately following (pp.17–18); proof §5.1

notes:
The binomial determinant uses the standard zero convention outside the binomial range. Even-N equality is not asserted; Table 2 gives computational evidence for N=4,6 and Problem 5.2 asks for even N≥8.
